newsitem.title: UK: Expert sees no De Beers contract in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Expert sees no De Beers contract in Russia.

text.p: A political power struggle in Russia makes it unlikely that South African diamond giant De Beers will conclude a new contract governing sales of rough Russian stones, a diamond trade expert told a conference here.
"The most likely outcome is that there will be no change in the present situation," John Helmer, the Moscow correspondent of trade magazine Diamond International, said Thursday.
But De Beers, which has been in talks for months to seal a final marketing deal, would hardly suffer, Helmer added.
"De Beers' position would not lose significantly if the current situation continues," he said.
De Beers, which controls about 75 percent of the world trade in rough diamonds, signed a memorandum of understandum with Russia in February.

The memorandum was to serve as a basis for a new contract to replace the deal dating from 1990, under which Russia sold most of its diamonds to De Beers' Central Selling Organisation (CSO) for marketing to polishing centres.
But a final agreement has recently been delayed by a goverment investigation against Almazy-Rossii Sahkha (ARS), Russia's main diamond producer and De Beers' negotiating partner.
The prosecutor-general's office accused ARS earlier this month of financial irregularities.

The government investigation is part of a struggle for control over the diamond proceeds between the regional government of Sahkha and the federal Russian government, Helmer told the conference on gold and diamond mining in the former Soviet Union.

As long as there is no new contract, the former deal, which officially expired in December 1995, remains in place. Under that contract, De Beer suffered from so-called "leakages": sales of Russian diamonds outside the CSO directly onto world markets.
But such sales now seem less of a problem for De Beers, Helmer said. "The threat of leakages has become less of a concern," he said.
